newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana airport plan delayed indefinitely - paper.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana airport plan delayed indefinitely - paper.

text.p: Funding problems will indefinitely delay a Louisiana project that called for an international airport, seaport, trucking and high-speed rail center between Baton Rouge and New Orleans, Advocate newspaper reported Tuesday.

Stephen Perry, chief of staff for Gov. Mike Foster, said the Federal Aviation Administration and Washington authorities had notified the state there was not enough federal funding available for the $2.35 billion project.
Perry said Louisiana could not build the project alone because of its self-imposed $200-million-a-year debt limit and because it has too many other needs.
"You don't really build an airport without federal support, and without federal support there's no way to do that from the state on its own. It's just financially impossible," Perry said.
The plan had been proposed by former Gov. Edwin Edwards but little had been said about it since Edwards left office in 1996.
